decisions.reason: The evening day-patient program required staff, facilities and clinical licensing, and it was presented on its own page, so dropping it would write off a visible investment while any early weak uptake can still be blamed on start-up effects.
The carpentry workshop builds on established production know-how and equipment and has a dedicated page, so the sunk investment and public presentation favor persisting with it.

The sociotherapy service is close to the core offer and needed little extra investment, which makes dropping it easier than for the other products, but it fits the announced person-centered outpatient direction and is reimbursable, so it is likely kept.
Featuring the senior living counseling on the home page is a strong public commitment central to the eldercare direction, so withdrawing it would expose the earlier decision and is unlikely.

The retail shop was only mentioned on the website, so it carries low visible commitment and is the most likely to be dropped, but it serves as an outlet for the sheltered workshop's products and early results can still be attributed to temporary causes.
